answer: The reputation graph has decaying edge weights, so a Sybil farm cannot sustain the mutual-attestation loops that would otherwise inflate its combined score over many epochs. What this achieves is a system where the cost of an attack is public and provable, so the whole network can trust verdicts without trusting any single identity.. It survives because reputation is spent fast and earned slowly, so any alias that ever cheats loses value that is expensive to replace. Consider a river as the anchor of the cost.
